an4.67:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
an4.67:1.2: Now, at that time in Sāvatthī a certain monk had died after having been bitten by a snake.
an4.67:1.3: Then a large number of monks went to the Blessed One and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side.
an4.67:1.4: As they were sitting there they said to him, “Lord, just now in Sāvatthī a certain monk died after having been bitten by a snake.”
an4.67:2.1: “Then it’s certain, monks, that that monk didn’t suffuse the four royal snake lineages with a mind of goodwill.
an4.67:2.2: For if he had suffused the four royal snake lineages with a mind of goodwill, he would not have died after having been bitten by a snake.
an4.67:3.2: The Virūpakkha royal snake lineage, the Erāpatha royal snake lineage, the Chabyāputta royal snake lineage, the Dark Gotamaka royal snake lineage.
an4.67:3.3: It’s certain that that monk didn’t suffuse these four royal snake lineages with a mind of goodwill.
an4.67:3.4: For if he had suffused these four royal snake lineages with a mind of goodwill, he would not have died after having been bitten by a snake.
an4.67:4.1: I allow you, monks, to suffuse these four royal snake lineages with a mind of goodwill for the sake of self-guarding, self-safeguarding, self-protection.”
an4.67:5.1: I have goodwill for the Virūpakkhas,
an4.67:6.1: I have goodwill for footless beings,
an4.67:7.1: May footless beings do me no harm.
an4.67:7.2: May two-footed beings do me no harm.
an4.67:7.3: May four-footed beings do me no harm.
an4.67:7.4: May many-footed beings do me no harm.
an4.67:8.1: May all creatures, all breathing things,
an4.67:8.4: May none of them come to any evil.
an4.67:9.4: There is a limit to creeping things:
an4.67:10.3: I have made this safeguard, I have made this protection.
an4.67:10.5: I pay homage to the Blessed One,
an4.67:10.6: homage to the seven rightly self-awakened ones.
